evidence.note: Built an fp64 ground-truth accuracy harness; compared bf16 vs tf32 multi-seed and at extreme Cauchy/large shapes, then edited the kernel — diagnosing a numeric-stability risk rather than nudging tolerances.

When the all-bf16 pipeline failed correctness, explicitly 'isolated the bf16 rounding source' and compared tf32-vs-bf16 projections with bf16 contraction, converging on a mixed-precision design (tf32 proj + bf16 contraction, fp32 tail). Classic root-cause-then-redesign of a numeric failure.

Repeatedly profiled the specific latency-bottleneck shapes (N=2048 dim=128, big dim=384 shapes) and targeted prologue/epilogue fusion, tiling, and streams there — distinguishing performance failures from correctness ones and attacking the true bottleneck.
Detected that integrating the fused epilogue broke correctness, retried, and produced a 'gated fused epilogue' that re-passed — re-verifying a fix and preventing a regression.

Extensive prologue variant sweep (2-dot/3-dot/split/interleaved/big-BM/no-transpose); evidence-driven but shows some circling, and little explicit 'stop optimizing this already-passing shape' reasoning, keeping it below the top anchor.

reasoning: The agent cleanly separates numeric failures (bf16 rounding under Cauchy/large-N) from performance failures (bottleneck shapes) and root-causes each with dedicated harnesses — fp64 comparison to isolate rounding, per-shape profiling to find the slow shapes — then redesigns precision strategy and tiling and re-verifies, even catching a regression the fused epilogue introduced (matching the level-8 anchor). It falls short of 10 because the exhaustive prologue microbenchmark churn borders on search rather than deliberate plan revision, and there is little explicit recognition of when a shape already clears the gate.
